description: The account's tracked keywords for an app — or across the whole portfolio — over any window: where each term ranked at the start and end, how far it moved, how many days it held and how many days it was measured, and optionally its day-by-day history, the same terms measured for named competitors, Search Visibility (a 0–100 score per storefront with the terms that moved it), and the terms two of your own apps are both on. Sorted worst movement first by default, so "what dropped" is at the top of a 300-term corpus — which also makes the returned rows a selection rather than a sample: `movers` and `coverage` are counted over the whole corpus and are what a summary comes from. Filter by `contains` to ask about one term by name. This is the tool for every question about tracked terms; it replaces get_tracked_keywords, get_keyword_positions and compare_keyword_positions.

app_id.description: Apptail app id for one of YOUR apps — get_account lists them. Required for `scope: "app"`. Not the numeric id in an App Store URL (that is apple_app_id).

compare_with.description: Apptail app ids to measure on these same terms — from get_competitors or search_apps. Rivals are measured on YOUR corpus, not theirs. At most 5 are used and the answer names which; send the ones that matter first.

contains.description: Only terms whose text carries this substring, matched case-insensitively and applied before the sort and the cap. This is how to ask about a term by name — "how is `mpg` doing" — without looking up its id first, and the only way to see a term that sits mid-table by movement and so never reaches the top of a sorted list.

country.description: Storefront to read ranks in (e.g. US, GB). Defaults to the app's primary storefront. Ranks only exist per storefront — the same term ranks differently in each — so one call answers for one market.

from.description: Start date, `YYYY-MM-DD`, inclusive. Overrides `period` when both are sent. Send it alone and the window runs to today.

include.description: Extra blocks. `history` adds a day-by-day series per term, capped at 25 terms — pair it with `keyword_ids` for specific terms. `visibility` adds **Search Visibility** — the 0–100 answer to "is our ASO working here", its like-for-like change and the terms that moved it, plus a line per storefront — and each row's `points_change` and `brand`; also the daily top-N counts, which are over every term the app appeared for, not over this corpus. `shared` adds the terms two of your own apps are both on, and needs `scope: "portfolio"`.

keyword_ids.description: Only these terms, by Apptail keyword id — from this tool's own output or discover_keywords. Ids the account does not track are still answered when the scope is one app, because "how is my app doing for this term" is a real question; the answer says so. Omit for the whole corpus.

limit.description: Max terms returned, after sorting. Default 100, capped at 300. The answer always says how many the corpus holds.

period.description: The window to report on. A calendar month as `2026-07`, a calendar year as `2026`, `last_month`, `this_month`, `last_year`, or a trailing window: `today`, `7d`, `14d`, `30d`, `90d`, `180d`, `365d`, `730d`, `1095d`. Defaults to `30d`. A calendar period is compared against the calendar period before it — July against June, not against the 31 days ending 30 June. Three years is the ceiling.

scope.description: `app` (the default) reads one app's corpus and needs `app_id`. `portfolio` reads every app the account owns and reports each term under whichever of them ranks best for it — that is the scope `include: ["shared"]` needs, and hidden apps are excluded from it.

sort.description: `movement` (the default) puts terms that left the results first, then real drops by size — the top of the list is what to ask about. `rank` is best position first, `volume` is most searched (Apple popularity), `competition` is most crowded. **Every sort selects, so a capped list is never a sample**: a movement-sorted read of 15 terms returns 15 movers whatever the corpus did. Count from `movers` and `coverage`, never from the rows.

tag_id.description: Only keywords carrying this tag. Tag ids come back on the keywords in this tool's own output. Omit for the whole corpus.

to.description: End date, `YYYY-MM-DD`, inclusive. Send it alone and the window is the three years before it.

name: get_keywords

app_ids.description: The apps these ranks were read for.

caveats.description: Sentences the reader has to hear before the list means what it looks like it means — a capped list and what it was selected for, terms nobody crawled, ranks that are weeks old, a history returned for only some rows, an include that did not apply. They carry the corpus-wide numbers in them so they survive being quoted alone. Pass these on; do not summarise them away.

compare_truncated.description: True when competitor ids were dropped for exceeding the cap of 5.

compared_app_ids.description: The competitor ids actually measured. Shorter than what was sent when the cap or an unknown id dropped one.

country.description: Storefront the ranks were measured in.

coverage.description: How much of this corpus was actually looked at in this window — the answer to "is this a drop or a gap in your crawling", which is otherwise unanswerable from ranks alone and has been guessed at wrongly. AppTail does not crawl every term every day, so sparse coverage on a few terms is normal; a corpus-wide `unmeasured` is not.

last_measured_on.description: The most recent day any term in this corpus was crawled, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Null when none were.

measured.description: Terms crawled on at least one day of the window.

ranked.description: Terms the app was in the results for on at least one day.

stale.description: Measured terms whose last crawl is more than `stale_after_days` before the end of the window. Their `current_position` is that older reading — true, and not news.

stale_after_days.description: The gap, in days, after which a term's last reading is counted as stale.

terms.description: Terms in the corpus after any filter.

unmeasured.description: Terms crawled on no day at all. Their rank fields are unknowns, not zeroes.

keywords.description: The terms, in the order `sort` asked for. **A selection, not a sample**: this is the top of a sorted list, so when `truncated` is true these rows are whatever the sort favoured — with the default sort, the worst movers and nothing else. Read them for which terms to ask about next; read `movers` and `coverage` for anything about the corpus. Empty when none are tracked in this storefront — track some with add_keywords.

app_id.description: The app these ranks belong to. On a portfolio-scoped call a term is reported under whichever of your apps ranks best for it, so this varies row to row.

best_position.description: The best rank held at any point in the window. -1 when the app never ranked. Says whether a term was ever winnable, which neither end of the window can.

brand.description: Whether this term is somebody's name, for Search Visibility. Present only with `include: ["visibility"]` at app scope.

kind.description: Null = scored. `own` = the app's own name; `competitor` = the name of the app ranking #1 for it. Either is listed and left out of Search Visibility.

override.description: The owner's decision, set with tag_keywords `brand`; `none` = counted whatever detection says. Null = detection decides.

reason.description: Why detection flagged it, e.g. "matches “Fuelio: MPG & Mileage Tracker”, which ranks #1".

competitors.description: Where the apps named in `compare_with` stood on this same term, measured on the same day as `current_position`. Empty when nothing was compared.

position.description: Its rank on the last crawled day, -1 for not ranking.

console_url.description: The keyword screen for the app this row belongs to.

country.description: Lowercase ISO code of the storefront this keyword is tracked in, e.g. "us". A term is tracked per country.

current_position.description: Rank on the last day in the window the term was crawled, 1 = top. **-1 means the app was not in the results on that day** — a real departure, not a gap — unless `days_measured` is 0, in which case nothing was measured and the -1 is an unknown. Not the last day of the window: most windows end on a day nobody crawled, and reading that literally reports every app as unranked. `last_measured_on` is the day this rank was read on; quote it whenever it is not recent.

days_measured.description: Days in the window the term was crawled at all — the honest denominator for `days_ranked`. Not the days in the window: the crawler does not visit every term every day, and measuring against days nobody looked would report a term that never moved as one that keeps dropping out. **0 means this term was never measured in the window**, so every rank field on the row is an unknown rather than a zero, and the term is counted in `movers.unmeasured` rather than in `held`.

days_ranked.description: Days in the window the app was in the results at all. Read against `days_measured`: a term held on 3 of 30 days is not a term you hold.

history.description: One entry per day in the window, oldest first, when `include: ["history"]` was asked for and this row was inside the cap. **Each day is one of three things and the entry says which**: a rank, `position: -1` with `measured: true` for a day the term was searched and the app was absent, or `position: null` with `measured: false` for a day nobody crawled. Only the middle one is a departure. Null for the whole field means the history was not asked for or not returned for this row — never that the app did not rank.

dynamics.description: What changed against the previous **measured** day, skipping over days nobody crawled. Null when the rank held, when the day was not measured, and on the first measured day of the window — which is a starting point, not an arrival.

delta.description: How many places the rank moved since the previous measurement.

status.description: "new" = entered the ranking, "out" = dropped out, "up"/"down" = moved.

measured.description: Whether the term was crawled on this day. False means AppTail has no reading for it — the gap is ours, not the app's. The crawler does not visit every term every day, so a sparse run of these is normal and says nothing about ranks.

position.description: Rank on this day, 1 = top. **-1 means the term was searched and this app was not in the results** — a real absence. **Null means nobody crawled the term that day**, which is not a rank at all: do not count it as a drop, do not average it in, and do not read a run of them as an app leaving the results. `measured` beside it says which of the two this is.

keyword_id.description: Apptail keyword ID. This is the `keyword_id` other tools expect.

last_measured_on.description: The last day in the window this term was crawled, `YYYY-MM-DD` — the day `current_position` was read on. Null when it was not crawled at all. **This is what tells a stale rank from a current one**: a term last measured three weeks before the window closed still reports the rank it held then, which is true and is not news. Say the date rather than presenting an old rank as today's.

movement.description: How the rank changed across the window. Null when it ended where it started — **and also when `days_measured` is 0**, where nothing was measured and there is no movement to report rather than a movement of nothing. Check `days_measured` before reading a null here as "steady".

delta.description: Places moved. Only meaningful when both ends are real ranks — for "new" and "out" it is measured against -1 and is not a number of places.

status.description: "up" = a better (smaller) rank than at the start, "down" = worse, "new" = did not rank at the start and does now, "out" = the reverse.

points_change.description: What this term did to Search Visibility in its storefront over the window, in points — its exact share of `visibility.score.change`, so the rows' values add up to it. Present only with `include: ["visibility"]` at app scope; null for a brand term, a term not measured in both weeks, or when visibility was not asked for.

popularity.description: Apple search popularity score (roughly 5-100). Higher means more searched. Null if not measured yet.

results_count.description: How many apps the store returns for this term. A rough competition signal: higher means more crowded.

start_position.description: Rank on the first day in the window the term was crawled, same scale. Compare with `current_position` for the direction of travel rather than a single snapshot.

store.description: Which store this keyword is tracked against.

tag.description: User-defined tag grouping this keyword, or null when untagged. Absent on portfolio-scoped calls: a tag belongs to one app's corpus, and two of your apps may tag the same term differently.

color.description: Tag colour as a hex code.

movers.description: The shape of the window in four numbers, **counted over every term in the corpus, not over the rows returned**. This is the only honest basis for a sentence about the corpus, and it is the one to lead with: 8 fell of 103 is a different week from 80 of 103, and a list of 15 rows cannot tell you which you are in.

fell.description: Terms that lost places or left the results in this window.

held.description: Terms that were measured and ended where they started.

of.description: Terms these four were counted over — the whole corpus after any filter, same as `total`. The four add up to it.

rose.description: Terms that gained places or entered the results.

unmeasured.description: Terms crawled on no day of the window. **Never folded into `held`** — a term nobody looked at has no rank to have held, and counting it as steady is a claim about our crawling dressed up as a claim about the app.

shared.description: Terms two of the account's own apps are both on, worst first, when `include: ["shared"]` was asked for at portfolio scope. Empty otherwise. Read `competing` before calling anything a conflict.

apps.description: The account's apps on this term, best rank first. Always at least two — a term one app is on is not shared.

app_id.description: One of the account's own apps.

established.description: Whether it has held the term for at least half the days anybody was measured on it. An app that arrived this week has not taken anything from anybody yet.

position.description: Its rank on the term, best first.

competing.description: Whether these apps are actually taking traffic from each other: two of them inside the top ten, in the same category, both established. **False is the default reading** — this accuses somebody's own portfolio of a problem and is deliberately slow to. A false here with a spread of 40 is a portfolio covering more ground, not a conflict.

country.description: Storefront the overlap is in. An overlap is per storefront, like every rank.

crawled_days.description: Days in the window the term was crawled at all — what `established` was measured against. Never the days in the window: a skipped crawl would otherwise read as an app that keeps dropping out.

keyword_id.description: Apptail keyword id for the contested term.

popularity.description: Apple search popularity. Read it first: a bad overlap on a term nobody searches is not a finding, which is why the list is ordered by this within each group.

popularity_pending.description: Whether `popularity` is null because nobody has asked Apple about this term yet. True means queued, not zero and not "Apple has no number for it" - do not read a null popularity as low popularity while this is true.

results_count.description: How many apps the store returns for the term.

same_category.description: Whether both apps sit in the same App Store category. A fuel tracker and a language app sharing "tracker" are two answers to two questions; an app whose category is unknown never counts as matching.

spread.description: Places between the best and worst of your apps on this term.

sort.description: The order the list came back in.

total.description: Terms the corpus holds in this storefront. Larger than `count` when the list was capped.

truncated.description: True when `count` is below `total`. Say the list is partial rather than reporting it as the whole corpus.

visibility.description: When `include: ["visibility"]` was asked for: Search Visibility (`score`, `storefronts`) and the daily band counts. **The band counts are not over this corpus**: they count every term the app appeared for that day in this storefront, tracked or not, so they move with whatever anybody crawled and can disagree with the rows (a corpus whose rows show 27 terms in the top 10 can read `top10: 20`). Read them as reach across the store, never as the corpus's state. Each is the last day with a row — a state, not a sum — and null when nothing has been rolled up. The whole block is null when visibility was not asked for.

change.description: Change against the window before this one, per band. **Null means no earlier day was rolled up** — no history, which is not a change of nothing.

overall.description: The app's Search Visibility across those storefronts, weighted by where its downloads come from (`weights_source`). **Lead with this for "is our ASO working" without a storefront in the question;** with one, lead with `score`. Null at portfolio scope or when the read failed.

change.description: The storefronts' like-for-like changes, weighted, over storefronts that have one. Null = no storefront had a baseline — not a change of zero.

compared.description: The apps in `compare_with` across storefronts — the console's competitor table column. Your weights, never theirs: their own download split is not yours to read, and a different weighting would not compare. Empty when nothing was compared.

app_id.description: Apptail id of the app from `compare_with`.

score.description: Its overall on YOUR non-brand terms, weighted by YOUR storefronts' `weight` — directly comparable with `score` above. 0 = nothing in the top 50 on them.

coverage.description: 0–1: the share of downloads the scored storefronts hold before rescaling. Low means the overall rests on a small part of where downloads come from. Null with equal weights.

effective_rank.description: The single place that earns this score on every term.

formula_version.description: Changes when the formula does; 1 now.

previous.description: The same weighting over each storefront's `previous`, over storefronts that have one.

reason.description: Why there is no overall score.

score.description: 0–100: the storefront scores weighted by each line's `weight`. Null when no storefront has a score — `reason` says why.

terms_scored.description: Non-brand terms across the storefronts that carry weight.

weights_month.description: YYYY-MM the weights belong to. They change only when the month does.

weights_source.description: `downloads`: each storefront's share of the app's App Store Connect downloads over the 90 days before `weights_month` began, rescaled over the scored storefronts and fixed for the month. `equal`: the app is not connected to App Store Connect on this account, or had no downloads in a scored storefront.

score.description: **Search Visibility** in the storefront asked about: 0–100, 100 = #1 on every non-brand tracked term, with its like-for-like `change`, the terms that moved it (`biggest_losses`, `biggest_gains`) and the rivals in `compare_with` scored on the same terms. **Lead with this for "is our ASO working"** — counting risers and fallers points the wrong way when a term at #1 drops to #7. Over every tracked term in the storefront, whatever filter the rows had. Null at portfolio scope (niches do not add up) or when the read failed — the caveats say which.

band.description: Banded on effective rank: dominant 60+ (≈#1–2 everywhere, owns the first screen), strong 35–59 (≈#2–4), visible 18–34 (≈#4–10), weak 9–17 (≈#10–25), invisible 0–8 (beyond #25). Null with `score`.

biggest_gains.description: The terms that added the most points, best first, at most 5.

place_now.description: Its place on the last day of the headline week. Null = not in the top 50 (it was measured).

place_then.description: Its place on the last day of the earlier week. Null = not in the top 50 (it was measured).

points_change.description: What it did to the score, in points. These add up to `change` across all terms.

biggest_losses.description: The terms that cost the most points, worst first, at most 5 — the answer to "why did it fall". Counted over the whole storefront corpus, whatever filter the rows had.

place_now.description: Its place on the last day of the headline week. Null = not in the top 50 (it was measured).

place_then.description: Its place on the last day of the earlier week. Null = not in the top 50 (it was measured).

points_change.description: What it did to the score, in points. These add up to `change` across all terms.

change.description: **Like-for-like** change in points: over the terms measured in both weeks only, so adding or removing terms cannot move it. Each row's `points_change` is its exact share. Null when the earlier week has no baseline — not a change of zero.

compared.description: The apps in `compare_with`, scored on this app's corpus — the same rule as the rows' `competitors`. Empty when nothing was compared.

app_id.description: Apptail id of the rival from `compare_with`.

score.description: Its score on YOUR terms, same weights, same weeks.

corpus_change.description: The list moving rather than the app. History is recomputed over today's list, so a term added last week still has its earlier places if anyone crawled it; only terms with no earlier crawl land here.

added.description: Terms scored now that were not measured in the earlier week.

effect.description: What they did to `score − previous`, in points. Never part of `change`.

removed.description: Terms measured in the earlier week that are not now.

country.description: The storefront this score is for.

effective_rank.description: The single place that would earn this score on every term: S = 21 is "as visible as ranking about #8 everywhere". The sentence to put beside the number. Null for no score or a score of 0.

formula_version.description: Changes when a constant behind the score changes; scores from different versions do not compare.

gained.description: Sum of the positive `points_change` — what the terms that improved added.

last_measured_on.description: The most recent full-depth crawl of any of these terms, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

lost.description: Sum of the negative `points_change`. `gained + lost = change`.

previous.description: The same score over the 7 days before the window began. `score − previous = change + corpus_change.effect`.

reason.description: Why `score` is null, with the fix — "Track 5 or more non-brand terms in DE to get a score". Null when there is a score.

score.description: 0–100: the app's weighted search places over the most its non-brand tracked terms allow. **100 = #1 on every one.** The mean of the last 7 days of the window. Null when fewer than 5 non-brand terms were measured — `reason` says why — and never 0 for missing: 0 is a measurement, nothing in the top 50.

terms_brand_excluded.description: Brand terms listed and left out: the app's own name (it ranks #1 whatever its ASO does) and rivals' names where that rival ranks #1. Detected from title words; an owner can override per term with tag_keywords `brand`. Rows carry `brand`.

terms_scored.description: Non-brand terms measured in the last 7 days — what `score` is over. Quote it beside the score.

terms_unmeasured.description: Non-brand terms with no full-depth crawl in the last 7 days. Out of this week's score — not counted as zero.

weeks.description: The two 7-day spans `score` and `previous` are over, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

storefronts.description: One line per storefront the app tracks terms in — score, change, band, weight — so "where is it working" is one call. Each is its own reading over its own terms; never add them up — `overall` weights them. Empty at portfolio scope.

change.description: Like-for-like change in points. Null = no baseline.

reason.description: Why there is no score here, with the fix.

terms_scored.description: Non-brand terms the score is over.

weight.description: 0–1: what this storefront counts for in `visibility.overall.score` (see `weights_source` there). Null = it has no score, so it is not in the overall.

window.description: The window actually read, which is not always the one asked for: an inverted range is swapped, a range past three years is shortened, and first-party figures are pulled back to the last day App Store Connect reported. Quote these dates, not the requested ones.

days.description: Length of the window in days.

label.description: What names this window — the period key, or `custom`.

title: Get Keywords
